findings.title: Escalation closure is not limited to the Runner's own fault kinds
findings.description: `_close_recovered` closes every open project escalation whose `fault_kind` is not in this tick's recurring set. It does not check that the kind is one the Runner raises (`FaultKind`). If any other component, such as the inbox or reconciliation in slices 123 and 124, raises a project escalation through `raise_project_escalation`, the Runner will close it on its first complete tick. It will record `closed_by="runner"` even though nothing recovered. Restrict the loop to kinds the Runner owns (`FaultKind` values), or filter on who raised the row. I did not check the store schema to see whether another raiser exists today.

findings.title: Project-scoped escalations keep only the first fault of each kind
findings.description: The store deduplicates on `(project, kind)`. If two runs go `launch_overdue` or `run_observation_failed` in the same project, only the first fault's `node_id`, `run_id` and `detail` reach the escalation. The second node's failure is invisible to the operator until the first clears. `TickFaults` holds every fault, so the loss happens when the rows are written. Aggregate the details into one payload, for example a list of nodes and run ids, or document that this is intended.

findings.title: Forward dependency on a partially initialised package
findings.description: `tick.py` does `from amoeba.runner import finish`. `amoeba/runner/__init__.py` imports `factory`, then `tenant`, then `tick`, so this runs while the package is still initialising. It works because `from pkg import submodule` falls back to importing the submodule. It is fragile, and a reordering of the `__init__` imports could break it. `from amoeba.runner.finish import record` is safer.

findings.title: Duplicated runner name and a non-`Final` constant
findings.description: `CLOSED_BY: str = "runner"` repeats `RUNNER_TENANT_NAME` in `tenant.py`. The project rules say a value is defined once. `CLOSED_BY` is also not declared `Final`.

findings.title: Loose typing at some seams
findings.description: `validate_settings` reads fields with `getattr(settings, name)` over string names, which pyright strict cannot check. `probe_sq` takes `poll: Callable[..., RunPoll]` and `PopenFactory` is `Callable[..., ChildHandle]`. The test support code adds many `# type: ignore` and `Any` uses, such as `crash_entry.py`'s monkeypatch of `Store.journal_resolve` and `observe_support.py`'s `on_call: Any`. The rules put test code under strict checking, so these should be narrowed over time.

findings.title: File size above guidance
findings.description: `observe.py` is about 326 lines, over the ~300-line guidance. `RunObserver` carries three per-entry dicts and sets (`_last_poll`, `_overdue`, `_faulted`). Splitting the unconfirmed-launch logic into its own module would shrink it.

findings.title: Process-boundary catch is documented and guarded
findings.description: The single `except Exception` has `# noqa: BLE001`. It logs with `logger.exception`, escalates, and re-raises store failures and `UpstreamShapeError` before reaching it. This matches rule (c). `test_the_runner_package_has_exactly_one_broad_except` enforces it by counting source text, which a comment containing the phrase would break. The test is brittle but acceptable.

findings.title: Crash-recovery and budget design
findings.description: The code journals the command before `Popen`. It blocks the node before resolving the entry, and both writes are idempotent on re-entry. Every subprocess call is gated by `TickBudget.allows_call`. SIGKILL tests cover each crash point. A budget-coverage test fails if a new call site skips the budget check. Tests use throwaway directories and a stub `sq` and `cf`, and none read a production URL variable. The import-boundary rules 10 and 11 are enforced by tests.

structured_findings.summary: Escalation closure is not limited to the Runner's own fault kinds
Project-scoped escalations keep only the first fault of each kind
Forward dependency on a partially initialised package
Duplicated runner name and a non-`Final` constant
Process-boundary catch is documented and guarded
